sources.publisher: eCFR, Office of the Federal Register

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2, Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information in Nonfederal Systems and Organizations
NIST SP 800-171A, Assessing Security Requirements for Controlled Unclassified Information (June 2018)
NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment Methodology, Version 1.2.1 (June 24, 2020)

scoring.summary: Start at 110 and subtract each NOT MET requirement's point value. The score can be negative.

rules.summary: A requirement is MET only when every applicable assessment objective is satisfied.
rules.quote: Not Met. One or more applicable objectives for the security requirement is not satisfied.

rules.summary: An objective assessed N/A counts as MET.
rules.quote: an assessment objective assessed as N/A is equivalent to the same assessment objective being assessed as MET

rules.summary: Each NOT MET requirement's value is subtracted from the maximum, which may produce a negative score.
rules.quote: For each requirement NOT MET, the associated value of the security requirement is subtracted from the maximum score, which may result in a negative score.

IA.L2-3.5.3.partial_label: MFA implemented for remote and privileged users only

rules.summary: IA.L2-3.5.3 and SC.L2-3.13.11 subtract 3 points when partially implemented and 5 when not implemented.
rules.quote: Two derived security requirements, IA.L2-3.5.3 and SC.L2-3.13.11, can be partially effective even if not completely or properly implemented

rules.summary: A current System Security Plan must exist, or the assessment cannot be completed. It carries no point value.
rules.quote: OSAs must have a System Security Plan (SSP) (CMMC security requirement CA.L2-3.12.4) in place at the time of assessment

rules.summary: Conditional status needs a score of at least 80% of the maximum (88 of 110).
rules.quote: The assessment score divided by the total number of CMMC Level 2 security requirements is greater than or equal to 0.8

rules.summary: Only 1-point requirements may go on a POA&M (plus SC.L2-3.13.11 when encryption is used but not FIPS-validated). Six requirements can never be deferred; they must be closed before assessment.
rules.quote: None of the security requirements included in the POA&M have a point value of greater than 1

rules.summary: Every POA&M item must be closed and confirmed by a closeout assessment within 180 days, or Conditional status expires.
rules.quote: The closing of a POA&M must be confirmed by a POA&M closeout assessment within 180-days of the Conditional CMMC Status Date

rules.summary: Final status requires every requirement to be MET, either at assessment or after POA&M closeout.
rules.quote: The OSC has achieved the CMMC Status of Final Level 2 (C3PAO) if the Level 2 certification assessment results in a passing score

rules.summary: A Level 2 assessment must be repeated every three years, with an annual affirmation of continuing compliance.
rules.quote: The Level 2 certification assessment process must be performed every three years.

rules.summary: A senior Affirming Official must affirm compliance in SPRS after each assessment, after POA&M closeout, and every year.
rules.quote: must affirm the continuing compliance of their respective organizations with the specified security requirement after every assessment, including POA&M closeout, and annually thereafter

consequences.summary: Contracts that require CMMC Level 2 cannot be awarded until Conditional or Final Level 2 status is achieved.
consequences.quote: Prior to award of any contract or subcontract with a requirement for the CMMC Status of Level 2 (C3PAO), the following two requirements must be met

consequences.summary: If Conditional status expires during a contract, standard contractual remedies apply and the company cannot win further awards that need Level 2.
consequences.quote: the OSC will be ineligible for additional awards with a requirement for the CMMC Status of Level 2 (C3PAO), or higher requirement

glossary.definition: Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification, the Department of Defense program that verifies contractors protect federal contract and controlled information.
Controlled Unclassified Information: government information that is not classified but must still be protected.
Federal Contract Information: information provided by or generated for the government under a contract and not intended for public release.
Supplier Performance Risk System, where contractors record assessment scores and affirmations.
Plan of Action and Milestones: the documented plan for closing requirements that are not yet met.
System Security Plan: the document that describes the system in scope and how each requirement is implemented.
CMMC Third-Party Assessment Organization, an authorized body that performs Level 2 certification assessments.
Federal Information Processing Standards; FIPS 140 validation confirms a cryptographic module has been independently tested.
Multi-factor authentication: signing in with two or more independent factors.
